title: Ground → Ice
subtitle: 1x → 0.5x
body: Ice type chart change: Ice now takes 0.5x from Ground It is weak to Ice.

title: Rock → Ice
subtitle: 2x → 1x
body: Ice type chart change: Ice now takes 1x from Rock To remove Ice's crippling weakness to Stealth Rock. Also, ice is often responsible for erosion alongside water- due to freezing water expanding, widening cracks and weakening stone. Ice remains 1x against Rock offensively, but I feel it really doesn't need a weakness to it.

title: Water → Ice
subtitle: 1x → 0.5x
body: Ice type chart change: Ice now takes 0.5x from Water Ice is solidified water, giving it an elemental relation to Water. Also, Water needed to be taken down a peg somehow.

title: Dragon → Ice
subtitle: 1x → 0.5x
body: Ice type chart change: Ice now takes 0.5x from Dragon It is weak to Ice. As well, many Dragon-types can use Fire moves, and with Ice's old weakness to Rock- a type which Dragons can also often use- it made Ice a very bad answer to Dragon, even though it's supposed to be useful versus it. This resistance is coveted for any type that has it.

title: Baby Pokémon Egg Gift
subtitle: Gift Pokémon · Jubilife City Trainer School · Lv. 1
body: Baby Pokémon Egg Gift Gift Pokémon Jubilife City Trainer School level 1 Talk to the Cowgirl in the Jubilife School to receive an Egg. The Egg will hatch into one of the following Pokémon at random: Pichu, Cleffa, Igglybuff, Togepi, Tyrogue, Smoochum, Elekid, Magby, Azurill, Wynaut, Budew, Chingling, Bonsly, Mime Jr., Happiny, Munchlax, Riolu, Mantyke. You can save before collecting the Egg and soft reset if you don't like the result.

title: #1 Bulbasaur, #4 Charmander, #7 Squirtle
subtitle: Gift Pokémon · Jubilife City Pokémon Center · Lv. 5
body: #1 Bulbasaur, #4 Charmander, #7 Squirtle Gift Pokémon Jubilife City Pokémon Center level 5 Talk to the Interviewer at the top left. Answer her questions correctly and win the battle. Bulbasaur will be the first Pokémon she gives you. Charmander will be the second Pokémon she gives you. Squirtle will be the third Pokémon she gives you. If your party gets full before all three are given, she'll stop and you can talk again to receive the rest.

title: #131 Lapras
subtitle: Gift Pokémon · Pastoria City · Lv. 35
body: #131 Lapras Gift Pokémon Pastoria City level 35 In one of the houses is an old lady. Agree to listen to her story. She'll give you a Lapras after she finishes.

title: #133 Eevee
subtitle: Gift Pokémon · Twinleaf Town · Lv. 5
body: #133 Eevee Gift Pokémon Twinleaf Town level 5 Complete the events as far as Lucas/Dawn telling you to speak to your mother. Speak to your mother and she'll suggest taking Eevee. Interact with the Poké Ball to get Eevee.

title: #137 Porygon
subtitle: Gift Pokémon · Eterna Galactic Building · Lv. 22
body: #137 Porygon Gift Pokémon Eterna Galactic Building level 22 Defeat Jupiter at the Eterna Galactic Building. Interact with the Poké Ball behind her to get Porygon.

title: #138 Omanyte, #140 Kabuto, #142 Aerodactyl, #345 Lileep, #347 Anorith, #408 Cranidos, #410 Shieldon
subtitle: Gift Pokémon · Eterna City · Lv. 20
body: #138 Omanyte, #140 Kabuto, #142 Aerodactyl, #345 Lileep, #347 Anorith, #408 Cranidos, #410 Shieldon Gift Pokémon Eterna City level 20 Go to the Underground Man's house, near the Pokémon Center in Eterna City. Talk to the female scientist to receive fossils for all of these Pokémon. Take the fossils to the museum in Oreburgh City to revive them.

title: #152 Chikorita, #155 Cyndaquil, #158 Totodile
subtitle: Gift Pokémon · Floaroma Town Pokémon Center · Lv. 15
body: #152 Chikorita, #155 Cyndaquil, #158 Totodile Gift Pokémon Floaroma Town Pokémon Center level 15 Talk to the Interviewer at the top left. Answer her questions correctly and win the battle. Chikorita will be the first Pokémon she gives you. Cyndaquil will be the second Pokémon she gives you. Totodile will be the third Pokémon she gives you. If your party gets full before all three are given, she'll stop and you can talk again to receive the rest.

title: #252 Treecko, #255 Torchic, #258 Mudkip
subtitle: Gift Pokémon · Oreburgh City Pokémon Center · Lv. 10
body: #252 Treecko, #255 Torchic, #258 Mudkip Gift Pokémon Oreburgh City Pokémon Center level 10 Talk to the Interviewer at the top left. Answer her questions correctly and win the battle. Treecko will be the first Pokémon she gives you. Torchic will be the second Pokémon she gives you. Mudkip will be the third Pokémon she gives you. If your party gets full before all three are given, she'll stop and you can talk again to receive the rest.

title: #374 Beldum
subtitle: Gift Pokémon · Oreburgh City · Lv. 10
body: #374 Beldum Gift Pokémon Oreburgh City level 10 Go inside the house near Oreburgh Mine. Talk to Steven and he'll offer you a Beldum.

title: #387 Turtwig, #390 Chimchar, #393 Piplup
subtitle: Gift Pokémon · Sandgem Town · Lv. 5
body: #387 Turtwig, #390 Chimchar, #393 Piplup Gift Pokémon Sandgem Town level 5 Interact with the briefcase at the top right of Rowan's lab. Rowan will say a few words and then allow you to take out the Poké Balls inside. Interact with the briefcase again to receive the two Sinnoh starters that you didn't choose. Turtwig, Chimchar and Piplup will be given in that order, with the one you did select not appearing.

title: #94 Gengar
subtitle: Special Encounters · Old Chateau · Lv. 20
body: #94 Gengar Special Encounters Old Chateau level 20 Talk to the painting with the glowing red ones in one of the rooms at the back of the Old Chateau. Attempt to leave the room and you'll encounter Gengar. This event can only be performed once.

title: #442 Spiritomb
subtitle: Special Encounters · Route 209 · Lv. 30
body: #442 Spiritomb Special Encounters Route 209 level 30 Get the Odd Keystone from a man on Route 208, hidden in Twinleaf Town or from the Underground. Talk to the broken stone tower to encounter Spiritomb.

title: #444 Gabite
subtitle: Special Encounters · Wayward Cave · Lv. 25
body: #444 Gabite Special Encounters Wayward Cave level 25 Go through the basement and up the stairs to the small room. Walk forward and you'll encounter Gabite. This event can only be performed once.

title: #479 Rotom
subtitle: Special Encounters · Old Chateau · Lv. 20
body: #479 Rotom Special Encounters Old Chateau level 20 Talk to the TV in one of the rooms at the back of the Old Chateau. The event is now repeatable and can be done at any time of day.

title: #144 Articuno
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Mt. Coronet (Summit) · Lv. 60
body: #144 Articuno Legendary Encounters Mt. Coronet (Summit) level 60 Speak to Rowan after the Distortion World events. Head to the snowy parts of Mt. Coronet. Bring something with Rock Climb. Just above the spiralling paths entrance is a portal. Talk to the portal to encounter Articuno. You can keep battling Articuno until you catch it.

title: #145 Zapdos
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Valley Windworks · Lv. 60
body: #145 Zapdos Legendary Encounters Valley Windworks level 60 Speak to Rowan after the Distortion World events. Head to Valley Windworks. Bring something with Surf. On an island behind the building is a portal. Talk to the portal to encounter Zapdos. You can keep battling Zapdos until you catch it.

title: #146 Moltres
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Victory Road · Lv. 60
body: #146 Moltres Legendary Encounters Victory Road level 60 Speak to Rowan after the Distortion World events. Head to Victory Road. Bring something with Rock Climb. In a small room accessible from the last big area is a portal. Talk to the portal to encounter Moltres. You can keep battling Moltres until you catch it.

title: #150 Mewtwo
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Oreburgh Gate · Lv. 70
body: #150 Mewtwo Legendary Encounters Oreburgh Gate level 70 After the credits, a portal will appear in the bottom floor of Oreburgh Gate. Once you gain access, talk to the nurse in the Battleground to receive the Odd Invitation. Go to Oreburgh Gate. Bring something with Surf. In the basement as far as in as you can go with Surf is a portal. Talk to the portal with the Odd Invitation in your inventory to encounter Mewtwo. You can keep battling Mewtwo until you catch it.

title: #151 Mew
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Route 201 · Lv. 40
body: #151 Mew Legendary Encounters Route 201 level 40 A Shroomish is in the top-left of Route 203 near some trees. Talk to it with an Oran Berry in your inventory. It'll take it, transform into Mew and disappear. After seeing the Shroomish part, you'll find a Buneary on Route 209 above a muddy slope. Talk to it with a Sitrus Berry in your inventory. It'll take it, transform into Mew and disappear. After seeing the Buneary part, you'll find a Torchic in Pastoria City on the alcove above the lake. Talk to it with an Old Gateau in your inventory. It'll take it, transform into Mew and disappear. After seeing the Torchic part, you'll find a Pachirisu on Route 201. Talk to it and it'll transform into Mew, but stay in place. Talk to Mew to encounter it. You can keep battling Mew until you catch it.

title: #243 Raikou
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Route 208 · Lv. 60
body: #243 Raikou Legendary Encounters Route 208 level 60 Speak to Rowan after the Distortion World events. Head to Route 208. Bring something with Rock Climb. On the platform on the left of the route accessible by Rock Climb is a portal. Talk to the portal to encounter Raikou. You can keep battling Raikou until you catch it.

title: #244 Entei
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Route 211 (East) · Lv. 60
body: #244 Entei Legendary Encounters Route 211 (East) level 60 Speak to Rowan after the Distortion World events. Head to Route 211 (East). Bring something with Rock Climb. On the platform on the top of the route accessible by Rock Climb is a portal. Talk to the portal to encounter Entei. You can keep battling Entei until you catch it.

title: #245 Suicune
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Route 213 · Lv. 60
body: #245 Suicune Legendary Encounters Route 213 level 60 Speak to Rowan after the Distortion World events. Head to Route 213. Bring something with Rock Climb. At the bottom of the platform in the middle of the route accessible by Rock Climb is a portal. Talk to the portal to encounter Suicune. You can keep battling Suicune until you catch it.

title: #249 Lugia
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Route 220 · Lv. 70
body: #249 Lugia Legendary Encounters Route 220 level 70 After the credits, a portal will appear on Route 220. Place Articuno, Zapdos and Moltres in your active party. Ask Professor Oak in Eterna City about 'Quests' to get the Silver Wing. Go to Route 220. Bring something with Surf. At the bottom of the route is a portal on a small island. Talk to the portal with the Silver Wing in your inventory to encounter Lugia. You can keep battling Lugia until you catch it.

title: #250 Ho-oh
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Lost Tower · Lv. 70
body: #250 Ho-oh Legendary Encounters Lost Tower level 70 After the credits, a portal will appear at the top of the Lost Tower. Do the Lugia quest as far as receiving the Silver Wing from Professor Oak. Place Raikou, Entei and Suicune in your active party. Ask Professor Oak in Eterna City about 'Quests' to get the Rainbow Wing. Go to the Lost Tower. On the top floor by a grave is a portal. Talk to the portal with the Rainbow Wing in your inventory to encounter Ho-oh. You can keep battling Ho-oh until you catch it.

title: #251 Celebi
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Eterna Forest · Lv. 40
body: #251 Celebi Legendary Encounters Eterna Forest level 40 Check the shrine in Celestic Town to get the GS Ball. After getting the GS Ball, return to Eterna Forest from the entrance on the Eterna City side. Walk forward and you should see a message saying the GS Ball is shaking, followed by several red portals appearing around Eterna Forest. Celebi will come out of the portal in sight, see you, then dive back in. Go to each of the portals and talk to them to do a small Trainer fight. There are eight in all. After all eight portals have been cleared, another red portal will appear close to the center of the forest. Talk to this red portal to encounter Celebi. You can keep battling Celebi until you catch it.

title: #377 Regirock
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Route 228 · Lv. 60
body: #377 Regirock Legendary Encounters Route 228 level 60 Complete the Distortion World events. Enter Route 228 with a Relicanth and Wailord in your party. Enter the cave entrance near the top of the route below the muddy slopes. Walk over each glowing tile and talk to the statue to encounter Regirock. You can exit and enter the room to encounter Regirock again until you catch it.

title: #378 Regice
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Mt. Coronet (Route 216 Entrance) · Lv. 60
body: #378 Regice Legendary Encounters Mt. Coronet (Route 216 Entrance) level 60 Complete the Distortion World events. Enter the Mt. Coronet room leading to Route 216 with a Relicanth and Wailord in your party. Enter the cave entrance at the top right of this room. Walk over each glowing tile and talk to the statue to encounter Regice. You can exit and enter the room to encounter Regice again until you catch it.

title: #379 Registeel
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Iron Island (B3F) · Lv. 60
body: #379 Registeel Legendary Encounters Iron Island (B3F) level 60 Complete the Distortion World events. Enter the Iron Island room leading to the exit above the ledge with a Relicanth and Wailord in your party. Enter the cave entrance at the top right of this room. Walk over each glowing tile and talk to the statue to encounter Registeel. You can exit and enter the room to encounter Registeel again until you catch it.

title: #380 Latias
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Fullmoon Island · Lv. 68
body: #380 Latias Legendary Encounters Fullmoon Island level 68 Speak to Steven in Oreburgh City via the Quests option with the Magma Stone in your inventory to receive the Soul Dew. Catch Cresselia on Fullmoon Island to get a rock to appear in the clearing. Talk to the clearing from its bottom with the Soul Dew in your inventory to get a choice. Choose "Red" to encounter Latias. You can pick "Red" to battle Latias repeatedly until you catch it.

title: #381 Latios
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Fullmoon Island · Lv. 68
body: #381 Latios Legendary Encounters Fullmoon Island level 68 Speak to Steven in Oreburgh City via the Quests option with the Magma Stone in your inventory to receive the Soul Dew. Catch Cresselia on Fullmoon Island to get a rock to appear in the clearing. Talk to the clearing from its bottom with the Soul Dew in your inventory to get a choice. Choose "Blue" to encounter Latios. You can pick "Blue" to battle Latios repeatedly until you catch it.

title: #382 Kyogre
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Mt. Coronet (B1F) · Lv. 70
body: #382 Kyogre Legendary Encounters Mt. Coronet (B1F) level 70 After the credits, a portal will appear in the basement of Mt. Coronet. Steven must have received the Magma Stone and been shown Latias and Latios. Talk to Steven in Oreburgh City via the Quests option with Regirock, Regice and Registeel in your inventory to receive the Blue Orb. Go to the basement of Mt. Coronet. Bring something with Surf. In the island in the center of the water is a portal. Talk to the portal with the Blue Orb in your inventory to encounter Kyogre. You can keep battling Kyogre until you catch it.

title: #383 Groudon
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Stark Mountain (Interior) · Lv. 70
body: #383 Groudon Legendary Encounters Stark Mountain (Interior) level 70 After the credits, a portal will appear in the first room of Stark Mountain's interior. Steven must have received the Magma Stone and been shown Latias and Latios. Talk to Steven in Oreburgh City via the Quests option with Regirock, Regice and Registeel in your inventory to receive the Red Orb. Go to the first room of Stark Mountain. To the left of the steps leading to the next room is a portal. Talk to the portal with the Red Orb in your inventory to encounter Groudon. You can keep battling Groudon until you catch it.

title: #384 Rayquaza
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Pokémon League · Lv. 70
body: #384 Rayquaza Legendary Encounters Pokémon League level 70 After the credits, a portal will appear at the Pokémon League below the waterfall. Steven must have received the Magma Stone and been shown Latias and Latios. Talk to Steven in Oreburgh City via the Quests option with Regirock, Regice and Registeel in your inventory to receive the Jade Orb. Go to the Pokémon League part above Victory Road. Below the waterfall on a small bit of land jutting out is a portal. Talk to the portal with the Jade Orb in your inventory to encounter Rayquaza. You can keep battling Rayquaza until you catch it.

title: #385 Jirachi
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Solaceon Ruins · Lv. 40
body: #385 Jirachi Legendary Encounters Solaceon Ruins level 40 Talk to the girl in the Pokemon Center in Eterna City with a Dazzling Gleam TM in your inventory. Talk to the old woman in a house in Solaceon Town below the ledges with a Ponyta, Rapidash, Moltres, Quilava or Infernape in your party. Talk to the little boy outside the bottom house in Pastoria with a Gyarados, Carvanha or Sharpedo in your party. Talk to the sign on the bottom floor of Solaceon Ruins. Talk to Jirachi wth a Jigglypuff in your party and select 'Yes' to singing to it to encounter Jirachi. You can keep battling Jirachi until you catch it.

title: #386 Deoxys
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Veilstone City · Lv. 70
body: #386 Deoxys Legendary Encounters Veilstone City level 70 After the credits, talk to any of the meteories in Veilstone City. You should receive a message about something getting angry. Enter the bottommost meteor pit that has two meteorites in it, past the steps. Go up the steps and exit the pit. A portal will appear behind you and Deoxys will rush out and battle you. You can exit from the meteor pit to encounter Deoxys repeatedly until you catch it.

title: #480 Uxie
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Acuity Cavern · Lv. 60
body: #480 Uxie Legendary Encounters Acuity Cavern level 60 Speak to Rowan after the Distortion World events. Go to Lake Acuity. Bring something with Surf and Rock Climb. Go to the island in the center and enter the cave. Talk to Uxie to encounter it. You can keep battling Uxie until you catch it.

title: #481 Mesprit
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Verity Cavern · Lv. 60
body: #481 Mesprit Legendary Encounters Verity Cavern level 60 Speak to Rowan after the Distortion World events. Go to Lake Verity. Bring something with Surf. Go to the island in the center and enter the cave. Talk to Mesprit to encounter it. You can keep battling Mesprit until you catch it.

title: #482 Azelf
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Valor Cavern · Lv. 60
body: #482 Azelf Legendary Encounters Valor Cavern level 60 Speak to Rowan after the Distortion World events. Go to Lake Valor. Bring something with Surf. Go to the island in the center and enter the cave. Talk to Azelf to encounter it. You can keep battling Azelf until you catch it.

title: #483 Dialga
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Spear Pillar · Lv. 70
body: #483 Dialga Legendary Encounters Spear Pillar level 70 After the credits, talk to the Celestic elder in the big house in Celestic Town. Go to Mt. Coronet. Surf, Waterfall and Rock Climb are required. Collect the Adamant Orb in the cave above the waterfall in the room accessible from the summit. Go to Spear Pillar with the Adamant Orb in your inventory and talk to the blue portal to encounter Dialga. If you defeat or run from Dialga, you will need to defeat the Elite Four to get it to appear again.

title: #484 Palkia
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Spear Pillar · Lv. 70
body: #484 Palkia Legendary Encounters Spear Pillar level 70 After the credits, talk to the Celestic elder in the big house in Celestic Town. Go to Mt. Coronet. Surf, Waterfall and Rock Climb are required. Collect the Lustrous Orb in the cave above the waterfall in the room accessible from the summit. You must have encountered Dialga and caught, ran or defeated it before you can encounter Palkia. Go to Spear Pillar with the Lustrous Orb in your inventory and talk to the pink portal to encounter Palkia. If you defeat or run from Palkia, you will need to defeat the Elite Four to get it to appear again.

title: #485 Heatran
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Stark Mountain (Furthest Room - Interior) · Lv. 68
body: #485 Heatran Legendary Encounters Stark Mountain (Furthest Room - Interior) level 68 After completing the Stark Mountain events, go to the Survival Area. Enter the Battleground and Buck's grandfather will talk to you. Return to the room furthest in Stark Mountain and Heatran will appear. Talk to Heatran to battle it. If you defeat or run from Heatran, you will need to defeat the Elite Four to get it to appear again. After you catch Heatran, you will receive the Magma Stone.

title: #486 Regigigas
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Snowpoint Temple (B6F) · Lv. 70
body: #486 Regigigas Legendary Encounters Snowpoint Temple (B6F) level 70 Complete the events in the story with Regigigas in the Snowpoint Temple. Become the Champion (ie see the credits). Go to the basement of the Snowpoint Temple with Regirock, Regice and Registeel in your party. Talk to Regigigas with Regirock, Regice and Registeel in your party to encounter it. If you defeat or run from Regigigas, you will need to defeat the Elite Four to get it to appear again.

title: #487 Giratina
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Distortion World / Turnback Cave · Lv. 70
body: #487 Giratina Legendary Encounters Distortion World / Turnback Cave level 70 Giratina is encountered in the Distortion World as part of the story. If you defeat or run from Giratina in the Distortion World, you can find it in the final room of Turnback Cave after the credits at Level 70. If you defeat or run from Giratina in Turnback Cave, you will need to defeat the Elite Four to get it to appear again.

title: #488 Cresselia
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Fullmoon Island · Lv. 68
body: #488 Cresselia Legendary Encounters Fullmoon Island level 68 After the credits, go to Canalave and into the house next to the port. Talk to the young boy in the bed. Talk to the sailor outside to go to Fullmoon Island. Talk to Cresselia in the grove further in the island to encounter it.

title: #489 Phione
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · N/A · Lv. N/A
body: #489 Phione Legendary Encounters N/A level N/A Place Manaphy in the Daycare in Solaceon Town with a Ditto as a partner. Once an Egg is found, take it and hatch it to get Phione.

title: #490 Manaphy
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Pokémon Mansion · Lv. N/A
body: #490 Manaphy Legendary Encounters Pokémon Mansion level N/A After the story events at the Pokémon Mansion, you will be offered an Egg. Accept the Egg, then hatch it to get Manaphy.

title: #491 Darkrai
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Newmoon Island · Lv. 68
body: #491 Darkrai Legendary Encounters Newmoon Island level 68 Obtain the Lunar Wing by capturing Cresselia on Fullmoon Island. Talk to the young boy in the house next to the port to heal him. Talk to the woman in the dark house on Route 217 to get the Member Card. Enter the top house in Canalave City to get warped to Newmoon Island. Talk to Darkrai in the grove further in the island to encounter it. You can fight Darkrai repeatedly by re-entering the house until you catch it.

title: #492 Shaymin
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Flower Paradise · Lv. 30
body: #492 Shaymin Legendary Encounters Flower Paradise level 30 Defeat Dawn or Lucas at Route 224 as part of the storyline. Talk to Professor Oak in Eterna City to receive Oak's Letter. Head to Route 224 and go towards the top of the route. Marley will speak to you. Speak to Professor Oak, and enter in whatever you want on the stone tablet. The map will change and Shaymin will appear, then flee. Head up the Seabreak Path towards the Flower Paradise. Talk to Shaymin in the center of the Flower Paradise to encounter it. You can fight Shaymin repeatedly by exiting and entering Flower Paradise until you catch it.

title: #493 Arceus
subtitle: Legendary Encounters · Hall of Origin · Lv. 100
body: #493 Arceus Legendary Encounters Hall of Origin level 100 After the credits, talk to the old woman in the 'Foreign Building' in Hearthome City to make the Type Master trainers appear. You need to collect all sixteen Plate items (the Pixie Plate has not been added). You can get the Plates via the Underground or by defeating the Type Master trainers. The Plates previously in the field have been removed. Type Master trainers must be challenged with only a single Pokémon on your team that shares the type they specialise in. Flame Plate: The Fire-type Type Master is found on Route 226, just right of the Survival Area. Splash Plate: The Water-type Type Master is found on Route 219, just below Sandgem Town. Zap Plate: The Electric-type Type Master is found in Sunyshore City, inside the lighthouse. Meadow Plate: The Grass-type Type Master is found in Floaroma Meadow, just right of the house. Icicle Plate: The Ice-type Type Master is found in Snowpoint City, to the right of the Gym. Fist Plate: The Fighting-type Type Master is found in Veilstone City, in the house just south of the Gym. Toxic Plate: The Poison-type Type Master is found in Pastoria City, on the top floor of the Great Marsh lobby. Earth Plate: The Ground-type Type Master is found in Oreburgh Gate, on the top floor north of the entrances. Sky Plate: The Flying-type Type Master is found at the Pokémon League, looking out on the right outside the building. Mind Plate: The Psychic-type Type Master is found in Solaceon Ruins, just inside the entrance. Insect Plate: The Bug-type Type Master is found on Route 202, just above the Sandgem Town entrance. Stone Plate: The Rock-type Type Master is found on Route 207, just to the right of the muddy slope. Spooky Plate: The Ghost-type Type Master is found in the Lost Tower, on the ground floor. Draco Plate: The Dragon-type Type Master is found in Celestic Town, inside the ruins. Dread Plate: The Dark-type Type Master is found in the Sendoff Spring, just after the entrance from Route 214. Iron Plate: The Steel-type Type Master is found on Iron Island, just south of the entrance to the cave. With all sixteen Plates in your inventory, talk to the old woman in the 'Foreign Building' to get your second task: Complete the Pokédex. Once your National Pokédex is completed to an extent that you're able to view the diploma in Valor Lakefront (i.e. you have obtained all Pokémon except for Mew, Ho-Oh, Lugia, Celebi, Jirachi, Deoxys, Phione, Manaphy, Darkrai, Shaymin, and Arceus), talk to the old woman again to receive the Azure Flute. Go to Spear Pillar and stand on the flute symbol just as you leave the cave. You'll be prompted to play the Azure Flute. Head up the stairs to battle Arceus. Be warned, this fight is now at least on par with Ultra Necrozma, if not tougher. Arceus is more durable than Blissey in both Defense and Special Defense, and the fastest Pokemon in the game. Come prepared... or just bring a Master Ball. You can fight Arceus repeatedly by playing the Azure Flute on the symbol until you catch it.

title: Why is the patching not working?
subtitle: FAQ
body: Q: Why is the patching not working? Make sure you're using the correct Platinum ROM. It should be listed as Revision 1, Rev 1, or the dump with the number listed as 4997 or 4998. The 3541 one does not work for this hack. Make sure you're trying to apply the patch to an .nds file (that should be 128 MB). It should not still be compressed in a .zip or .7z, and it definitely should not be an .exe! If you are on Mac, consider using a program called MultiPatch instead (easy to find on Google). The Delta Patcher Lite tool will probably not work for you. Patching is a bit unreliable on mobile phones. I can't really help with problems there.

title: Why has my game frozen when trying to start the first rival battle?
subtitle: FAQ
body: Q: Why has my game frozen when trying to start the first rival battle? This means you've likely used the wrong ROM base. Most websites have the correct Platinum dump listed as 4997 or 4998. There is an earlier copy listed as 3541 - this will not work. If you try to force the patch through by unchecking "checksum validation" in Delta Patcher Lite, you will probably also end up with this issue. If you have the correct ROM base, you won't need to uncheck the "checksum validation".

title: How can I update my Altered Platinum to a newer version?
subtitle: FAQ
body: Q: How can I update my Altered Platinum to a newer version? Altered Platinum save files are compatible between each version, so this should be possible. Most emulators link the ROM name and the save file together, e.g. AlteredPlatinum.nds would have a corresponding save file AlteredPlatinum.sav. Please note I am referring to battery (normal) saves here done by the save menu in game. ** Save states will NOT work if you change the ROM version! ** First, get an .nds copy of the newest Altered Platinum. The patch must always be applied to a vanilla Platinum ROM. Export / Import Battery Saves (DeSmuME) If using DeSmuME, you can export your current battery save by going to File -> Export Backup Memory in DeSmuME to produce a .sav file. Do this while playing the old Altered Platinum with your current save file loaded. Open the new ROM, then do File -> Import Backup Memory and select the .sav you just exported. Your save file should now be active. The Filename Switch Method Rename the new version of the Altered Platinum ROM have the same filename as whatever your now old version file is. For example, if you were playing AlteredPlatinumX.nds on your emulator, and your new version is now AlteredPlatinumY.nds, you could rename that newer version from AlteredPlatinumY.nds -> AlteredPlatinumX.nds. Replace your old ROM with the new ROM. Boot up the new ROM on the emulator and hopefully your save file should be there. Please note that if you are updating from v1.0.0, v1.0.1, v1.0.2 or v1.0.3 to any newer version while keeping your save file, you will need to talk to the NPC found in any of the Pokémon Centers in Jubilife, Eterna, Hearthome or Veilstone to get everything in place in your save.

title: Can I randomise Altered Platinum?
subtitle: FAQ
body: Q: Can I randomise Altered Platinum? No, this is not possible via the Universal Pokémon Randomizer. Expanded files mean the internal file locations are different to normal, and the Universal Pokémon Randomizer is unable to handle this. This is impossible to add support for.

title: Can I get <Pokémon name here> as a shiny?
subtitle: FAQ
body: Q: Can I get <Pokémon name here> as a shiny? Yes, all Pokémon are available as shiny at the new shiny rate(1/512). You need to soft reset to try to get shinies for static encounters; save states don't reroll the RNG so you'll get the same Pokémon every time.

title: I'm seeing graphical distortion when walking in grass sometimes. Is this a bug?
subtitle: FAQ
body: Q: I'm seeing graphical distortion when walking in grass sometimes. Is this a bug? This is a bug, but not with the hack; it's a problem with the emulator (specifically DeSmuME that I know of). The graphical distortion is harmless and will go away when the screen is refreshed. This problem also happens with the original Platinum.

title: I finished the Galactic events in Eterna City and am now stuck. What do I do?
subtitle: FAQ
body: Q: I finished the Galactic events in Eterna City and am now stuck. What do I do? Go to the Bike Shop in Eterna City and talk to the owner. After this, you should be able to progress past Route 206.

title: Why can't I get into Canalave City? Where am I meant to go?
subtitle: FAQ
body: Q: Why can't I get into Canalave City? Where am I meant to go? You must now visit Pal Park before you can continue into Canalave City. Be sure to talk to all of the NPCs at Pal Park. You're after a specific item to get past the guard blocking you!

title: Pokémon Changes
subtitle: PokemonChanges.txt
body: Pokémon Changes PokemonChanges.txt Per-Pokémon type, base stat, ability, held item, evolution and learnset changes. General Changes - The Fairy-type has been added to the game, replacing the almost unused ???-type. - All Pokémon have had their base stats updated to match Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon. - All Pokémon have had their types updated to match Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon. - All Pokémon have had their wild held item updated to match Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon (with some exceptions). - All Pokémon now have an egg cycle of 0, i.e. they will hatch extremely quickly. - Wingull, Pelipper and Torkoal have gained their new abilities from Gen VII. - Pokémon that evolved with items which could no longer learn moves on level up now have full level-up sets. This was changed since I personally never liked this mechanic, as it meant you might have to wait a long time with an underpowered Pokémon just to get the move you want. This is dissimilar to the Pokémon which previously evolved with held items during a trade, which can use their items now with no strings attached. I feel consistency with these Pokémon is the best option, and it makes them easier to train. Effort Value Removal Effort Values are completely gone. Just entirely absent. This was done for a variety of reasons- the difficulty of this hack is intended to be based on tactical decisions, teambuilding and things like that- not on being a munchkin and trying to create the ultimate life-form. As well, opposing trainers can't use EVs anyway, so it's more balanced this way. You no longer have to worry about accidentally EV training your Jolteon with Attack and HP EVs, and such. IVs and natures are comparatively less impactful, and with Synchronize desirable natures can still be acquired if you really want them. With non-optimal IVs/Natures, your Pokémon have a marginal disadvantage, but the AI, even at max level, isn't the smartest anyway, so it can be thought of as a sort of handicap to make the trainers more dangerous. Held Item Exceptions - Pokémon who may hold an item in Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon that doesn't exist in Platinum will not hold anything. - Corsola has a 5% chance to hold a Hard Stone. - Pelipper has a 5% chance to hold a Lucky Egg. - Sinnohan Absol has a 5% chance to hold a Life Orb. - Spiritomb has a 100% chance to hold a Smoke Ball. Other Changes - Some Pokémon have ability slots flipped (e.g. Scizor). This is because enemy Trainers always use the first ability. - The rate for Shiny Pokémon is now 1/512, instead of 1/8192. - Many of the shiny Pokémon I thought looked hideous have had entirely new palettes added. Some I've changed just because I wanted to, but a large majority of shinies are unchanged. Either because I doubt most people care about them, or because I already like them enough. All starters except Venusaur, Charizard and Meganium have new shinies, though! Also- Onix and Steelix are based on the Crystal Onix from the anime! Ability changes Several abilities have been renamed so that they can apply to more Pokémon. The purpose of this is to increase ability variety, by adding 'new' clone abilities(like Huge Power/Pure Power) with a more general concept, so more Pokémon can benefit. Generation 4 has a lack of abilities I would like to implement if it was possible, so this is a nice compromise. All of these abilities do exactly the same thing- the rename is only meant to make them fit on more Pokémon. Clear Body has been renamed to Strong Body. New description: "Its toughness prevents stat reduction." New users: Hitmonchan, Pinsir, Heracross, Skarmory, Whiscash, Armaldo, Piplup/Prinplup/Empoleon, Snover Download has been renamed to Instinct. New description: "Boosts an offense based on foe's weakness." New users: Nidoking, Voltorb/Electrode, Sceptile, Kecleon, Deoxys, Mothim, Lucario, Toxicroak, Sinnohan Furret Compound Eyes has been renamed to Deadeye. New description: "Amazing senses boost its accuracy." New users: Pidgeot, Seel, Dewgong, Starmie, Persian, Kecleon, Sinnohan Scyther, Sinnohan Flygon Rock Head has been renamed to Determined. New description: "Its sheer determination prevents recoil damage." New users: Charizard, Tauros, Flareon, Ursaring, Blaziken Own Tempo has been renamed to Simple Mind. New description: "Its clear thoughts prevent confusion." New users: Primeape Sturdy has been entirely removed from the game, as one-hit KO moves no longer exist. Lightning Rod and Storm Drain have also been entirely removed from the game. This is because in Gen 4, they lack their Electric/Water immunity attributes, as well as the Special Attack boost, and ONLY redirect these moves during double battles, making them ludicrously terrible. Most instances have been replaced with Volt Absorb/Motor Drive and Water Absorb. Custom Changes From the bases as listed above, further changes to any Pokémon are listed below. These can include changes to base stats, abilities, types etcetera. Some Pokémon have had a Hidden Ability from a later generation added as a regular ability (e.g. Torkoal). TM compatibilty with any of the new TMs (Bug Buzz, Hurricane) is also listed here. Any move previously unavailable to a Pokémon is listed with a (!!) besides it. If a move was added to a Pokémon because of Pokémon Legends: Arceus, it will be listed with a (PLA) besides it. Level up moves have also been changed for every single Pokémon. These should include all moves they learn in Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon that are available in Altered Platinum, as well as additional moves from move tutors, egg moves or entirely new techniques. Each Pokémon is listed under its own section header below. Specific Changes

title: Sinnohan Forms
subtitle: SinnohanForms.txt
body: Sinnohan Forms SinnohanForms.txt The 65 Sinnohan regional forms: types, abilities, stats, evolutions and learnsets. General Notes - Sinnohan Forms are new regional variants with the same general concept as Alolan Forms- new type, abilities, stats and moves. Unlike Alolan Forms, though, they totally replace the originals, due to engine limitations. They also cannot breed. There are a total of 30 Sinnohan Forms- three times the number of Alolan Forms, and 10 per region prior to Sinnoh. None of these have been rushed, and were completed gradually over a long period of time as new ideas came in. Though some might be a little overpowered, they were designed to be mostly balanced(compared to the new standard of power). It's singleplayer anyway, so it's not like it matters too much! A large blank space has been added below in case you decide to avoid spoilers. Sinnohan Forms

title: Type Changes
subtitle: TypeChanges.txt
body: Type Changes TypeChanges.txt The Ice type-chart rework and the 69 Pokémon type changes with justifications. General Changes Fairy-type is now in the game, replacing what was previously the ??? type. All Pokémon that are Fairy-type in Gen VI onwards are also Fairy-type in Altered Platinum. Rotom's five alternate forms take the secondary type that they have in the Gen V games and onward (they are not Ghost-type like the normal Platinum). As in Generation VI games and onward, Steel takes 1x damage from Dark and Ghost attacks. Some fossil Pokemon are no longer Rock-type. If I think the type benefitted them, it remained. Ice Type Changes - Ice is the only type which has had its relations changed from vanilla- this is because I feel Ice is a grossly underpowered type. - The changes made were chosen both for thematic and gameplay reasons. Ice's resistances do not nerf already-underpowered offensive types. - With these changes, Ice is still weak to the common Fire and Fighting, plus Steel, but its key resistances to popular attacking types give Ice a real chance to take on a defensive role. Ground, Water and Dragon are very common offensive types without a lot of competition- and they are all, at least on offense, perhaps better than they deserve to be. With Ice resisting these, but still being weak to a couple of popular types as before, it is balanced out, and allows for more interesting things to be done with the type as a whole. - Keeping type chart changes limited to Ice also makes it easier to remember.

title: Wild Pokémon
subtitle: WildPokemon.txt
body: Wild Pokémon WildPokemon.txt Wild encounters by area, method and time of day. General Changes The Wild Pokémon in each area have been modified. The levels listed for an area are the minimum and maximum levels that you may encounter in that area. Please note that many Pokémon can only be encountered at one specific level. Only some have the range. Fishing rod encounters have levels based on area. The different rods have been replaced by Lures, new items obtained and used in the same way, which do not change level, but instead change what Pokémon you encounter. The Worm Lure and Berry Lure are obtainable from the same places as the Old Rod and Good Rod, respectively. The Fish Lure is obtainable in Snowpoint City. While the lures are meant to attract certain kinds of Pokémon, small, closed off bodies of water have only a limited range of different species. Oceans, rivers, and cave lakes connected to underground rivers have the widest variety. Lakes are average, and isolated ponds are the least varied. Honey trees now respond with an encounter straight away after applying Honey. Please note that the shiny rate for Pokémon is 1/512. Some Pokémon are only found when using the Poké Radar (these are listed as Poké Radar). These Pokémon may show up when you enter the patches with the yellow sparkles (NOT the shiny sparkles, that's something else!) Sinnohan Forms are marked by an (S) after the Pokémon's name. Note that they replace the originals, however, so this is only for convenience.
